reviews.text: If you're going to work with DS/ML people ever, this is pretty key/foundational to being able to speak their language. It's one of those classes where you have to lock in and fully pay attention the whole time and you'll learn a lot -- if you're half-listening, you won't get much out of it since it's pretty technical. Like 1/3 of the content is about how AI models work which isn't tested, which bothered some people, but I feel like it showed how the prof was just in it for the love of the game and teaching actually relevant/cool info about how AI models work so you can be kinda informed.

Terrific professor who explain concepts concisely, brings in relevant industry experience from the private sector in solving problems. Great energy so class is never boring. Fits into schedule well given the A/B term structure

This class basically teaches you how to navigate giant corporate bureaucracy and get your ideas through to execution, which is incredibly important. There were useful tips about innovation and convincing leaders in a way that challenged a lot of our thinking -- your initial instinct isn't always the most effective, and it's worth taking time to communicate an idea properly so that it actually gets traction. Some topics of the course felt a bit randomly incorporated, but tbh I still found it all pretty useful. Note that this is not a class on current innovations in tech, some examples feel outdated, but that's kind of fine because it's about the principles you learn from it

Super relevant, topical class. Interesting topics, interesting guest speakers. As someone who already worked in digital marketplaces, it was a bit repetitive/slow for me, but other people were obviously locked in and enjoying it, and I still learned stuff

This class is entirely group project based, so YMMV based on how good your group is (I got super lucky, so make sure to ask your friends which companies they are ranking so you get paired with people you know you work well with). It's really cool to get to apply PM concepts in practice and fill in any skill gaps you have with real experience with a real, cool company. I had been scared of the workload, and this class is not for someone looking to skate by because your reputation is on the line with a real company, but that being said, you're not killing yourself with tons of hours outside of class, it's manageable.
RE testing out of regular Product Management and jumping straight to this -- maybe only if you were a legitimate PM in title for years. If you were PM-adjacent, I still found it really helpful to take the intro to PM class first since that was all the concepts, and then Digital PM Lab is not that much lecturing, it's mostly applied + time for group project work in class.
It's more hands-on working with various companies on their real problems. Best recommended for folks, who have some PM exposure either through work
Really hands on class where you get to work with a client and solve a problem and go through the steps of being a PM. You also rank the options, so the p

You get out of this class what you put into it. While the main terminology can be learned from books, Prof Malek creates a sandbox for hands-on AI experimentation. It works well as an approachable entry point for beginners, while giving more experienced students the opprtunity to dive deeper into evals, RAG architecture, and agentic workflows.

Easy workload and content is presented in a very straightforward way, however if you are at all following the AI industry or familiar with AI tools you will probably find a lot of this class too high level

Canetti is a CBS Icon and I felt like class was the perfect balance of practicing fundamentals, and thinking AI-forward. Designed to teach the basics so you can recognize what is "good", understand and appreciate the work that goes into it, and prompt AI to actually do it right. 6-9:15 is always brutal but I felt like it was worth it for him. He also has cool startup experience that he talks about, applying his knowledge

Highly recommend if you have minimal SQL experience. The class is half asynchronous (videos) and half in person. I really enjoyed the format, because it let me work through SQL on my own before class, and then reinforce those learnings in person, where the professor walks through the logic step by step. Prof. Griffel is energetic and explains concepts very clearly. The course load is very manageable as long as you keep up with the lectures.

Prof is hilarious. Iconic class at CBS. Be prepared to be cold-called. Sometimes feels like you're not learning much / he can spend too much time soliciting participation, but he always brings it back to a framework or lesson at the end. Very much like Strategy core
Both parts entertaining & educational, although fair warning half the course is old school manufacturing related cases, so if that stuff bores you, the middle part will be hard to sit through

Amazing class and worth the 6pm if you are interested in AI Org Transformation. Super cool adjunct prof who was C-Suite at Atlassian and CBRE. We talked about what's happening in AI each week and had real frameworks on how to change and organization to adopt AI and the barriers to do so. Each week's homework was a podcast with super interesting industry perspectives. Final papers actually helped you apply the concepts.

There's no analytics, it's all foundational people management skills like hiring, employee motivation, etc. It's a shame I can't rec this class highly because I actually think these are really important skills everyone should know, it's just that the prof was dry and his delivery could be stiff/halting, which made some lectures hard to stay engaged with. The readings and concepts were helpful to me as someone who wants to be more intentional about people management, but basic to anyone who worked in HR. If you're interested in this topic like I was, I don't regret taking it, and it's pretty light workload

LOVED this class. Critical to take if you're entering tech from a non-tech background, and still helpful to fill in foundational gaps even if you do have a tech background. Fun group project (but note you are assigned to teams randomly so YMMV), engaging lectures and convos, and relevant homeworks.
Good overview course, especially liked the role-playing exercises and group projects. Some of the content did feel a bit hand-wavey at times

One of the best intro classes I've ever taken. Professor is extremely engaging & funny and really made the lectures easy to pay attention to. Much of the course load was group work based, so if you hate group work, do NOT take this class. The group work focuses on developing on one product feature for a company, and every single group is based on lectures where you now get to put it into practice, so I found that super helpful as someone with a non-PM background. He brings a couple speakers in which were either a huge hit or miss but I liked that it changed things up throughout the semester! Would definitely take another course with him.

Great foundation class for aspiring PMs and the professor has extensive experience in GTM strategy and product from LinkedIn and Reddit. Strongly Yes for professor and class! The block week format was quite fast so you could consider the full semester version if you wanted to dig deeper.

Exposure to important concepts (leveraging APIs, pandas dataframes, etc) and the later assignments are really open ended so you can choose what you want to teach yourself for them (I used the Anthropic SDK for the last two even though it was never covered in class / required in the assignment)

LOVED this class. Super relevant topics to intellectually engage with. The assignments used philosophical frameworks which at times felt pedantic but was probably the best way to objectively analyze hairy ethical situations. Really engaging professors and fascinating guest speakers.

Great class speakers! It was a great way to learn more about the ethical tensions that product managers think about and how the industry brainstorms solutions. I also enjoyed the coursework - it was great to partner in group work with newfound friends.

Pros: There were some good guest speakers, and the case topics covered a good range of businesses
Cons: I felt that the class discussions weren't that fruitful due to the focus on theoretical ethical frameworks and somewhat unfocused moderation of the conversation by the instructors. Also don't expect a typical case based class where there is a nice resolution to the challenge at hand--many of the business problems discussed are ongoing and/or opaque to outside parties, so in that sense I found it hard to take away concrete ideas from each case

The class will make you think about the other side of doing projects with AI:
-The types of data storage (cloud, client, on premise etc)
-The privacy aspect, no data stored or used for training etc
-Costs per token, costs as the solution scales etc.

Its good to know and think about these, but the class can be heavy and rough at times with boring cases

I'm the TA for growth hacking 😇 I think it's a great class. You get out what you put into it; it helped me get my internship because it was so applicable to real GTM work. Also Ross is a great professor!
i'd recommend building the sales machine rather than entrepreneurial selling. one of the better classes in general and super applicable

reviews.course: Launch Your Startup II, Growth Hacking, Entrepreneurial Selling
reviews.text: Launch your startup II should be available next semester! Also recommend Growth Hacking. I hear Entrepreneurial Selling is good, haven't taken that though
highly recommend the Building The Sales Machine class for those in GTM/revops space! but i think it's just offered in Spring!
insanely good class especially for anyone with 0 experience in a sales role / organization
Highly recommend FP&A or accounting for consultants (it's the same class, just half term vs full term)
Huge fan of Accounting for Consultants, definitrly do Cap Markets

reviews.course: Brand Management in the Digital Age, Economics of Strategic Behavior, Product Management
reviews.text: highly recommend Brand Management in the Digital Age, Economics of Strategic Behavior, Product Management
^ESB is a great class. with Wouter Dessein  and Prego both great
Also recommend Managerial Decision-making if you want a fluffy class that is still helpful (although I heard Timko is more aggressive than the Prof I had, but still very good).
Foundations of Business Law with Donna is great if you want a crash-course on the US legal system
Managerial Negotiations has been my favorite so far.
FP&A I think also is quite useful

reviews.course: Psychology and Economics of Consumer Finance
reviews.text: Another block week class I recommend (that's interesting, easy, and relevant) is Psychology and economics of consumer finance

I think Managerial Negotiations is pretty useful! It does feel a little fluffy at times but it helps you become more comfortable with negotiating in general (esp things I was too scared to negotiate before)
Leaders Voice with with Brad Aspel now and recommend!
Recommend Catching Growth Waves!! Prof Kohli is great
Python for MBAs: Mattan Griffel is the man and he founded the course.  Two time YC founder and is an incredible teacher with multiple cbs awards. Unclear if he still teaches it
Database course also rocked with Griffel. Generally speaking both classes give you a great foundation to unlock vibe coding

reviews.course: George Lentzas's AI and machine learning classes
reviews.text:
If you guys want to actually learn how modern AI works (ML foundations, deep neural nets, transformers, CNNs, RNNs, etc etc) I highly recommend taking the following classes with George Lentzas. NOT easy classes, but you will learn a ton of very useful knowledge and he brings cool speakers. As a dual degree taking engineering classes as well, I can honestly say these were even more useful than engineering classes themselves sooo, if you're serious about understanding how AI really works, go for it! it's old school teaching style, in class there's no phones, no laptops, he's very strict about it. Then in class it's theoretical + math and homeworks are applied, so let's say you spend one class learning about CNNs and then the HW is training your own CNN using PyTorch. During add/drop...maybe they are not in coursematch because they're technically part of MS program...or you'd have to get some sort of waiver in the system.
+ I second that, best class I have taken at cbs, but also the hardest
+ It should be called MS Machine Learning / MS Artificial Intelligence
+ Proceed with caution- it is a very heavy workload and you will be required to do coding and some math (like matrix multiplication or derivatives) by hand
Generative AI for Business is a good elective! BA core is a good headstart

If you're still looking for courses to rank in CourseMatch, I highly recommend taking Tech Ethics! It's co-taught by Chris LaSala and Jeremy Ney, who works in privacy at Google. The class is a great mix of cutting-edge case studies and top-notch speakers, with a really balanced way to examine the tradeoffs involved in AI and tech development. I am admittedly biased bc I took this last year (and am the TA this year 😉), but it's truly one of the best classes I've taken here
